chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Yusuf al-Baghdadi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Fadl al-Ahwazi narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Ahmad al-Qasri narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: My father Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all).

He said: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Talha, al-Zubayr, Sa'd, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, along with others from the Companions, went looking for the Prophet in the house of Umm Salama. They found me sitting at the door and asked me about him. I said, 'He will come out shortly.' He did not delay before coming out, and he struck my back with his hand and said: 'Great is [your status], O son of Abu Talib! For you will contend with the people after me regarding six qualities, and you will prevail over them, none of which exist among the Quraysh. Indeed, you are the first of them in faith in Allah, the most steadfast in carrying out Allah's command, the most fulfilling of Allah's covenant, the most compassionate towards the subjects, the most knowledgeable regarding judicial rulings, the most equitable in division, and the most superior in the sight of Allah, the Exalted.'
ai.seo_question: What are the six qualities in which Imam Ali (as) surpassed the Quraysh according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith highlights the Prophet’s specific designation of Ali ibn Abi Talib’s superiority in six distinct virtues, emphasizing that these qualities were unique to him and not shared by the Quraysh. The six attributes—faith, adherence to God’s command, covenant fulfillment, compassion, judicial knowledge, and equitable distribution—serve as a theological foundation for Ali’s preeminence in Shia scholarship, particularly regarding his role as the ideal ruler and judge. This narration is often cited to counter claims of equality among the companions, asserting Ali’s distinct spiritual and administrative excellence.
